scope: Proposition 7.6 (Higher estimates) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 78. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the entry bounds of Proposition 7.3 and the low estimates on smooth finite past diamonds. 1. On every fixed finite diamond, all fixed ordinary coordinate derivatives of γ±1, log A, b, a−1∂y1 b have finite bounds depending only on the corresponding smooth initial norms, the low bounds, and that diamond. 2. If the solution and its uniformly summed low estimates are defined on the full wedge, fix U ∈ R, C > 0, and either labeling {d, l} = {0, 1}. On s ≥ 0, yd ≤ U, yl ≤ CT, (7.37) every fixed ordinary coordinate derivative of γ±1, log A, b, a−1∂y1 b is bounded by eo(T). The same bounds hold on all restrictions and coordinate-path subsegments of this domain. Neither conclusion requires any higher-order initial norm to be small.
